transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Liam. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Liam, my name is Faisal Qureshi. I upgraded to your Hub Pro router yesterday, and now none of our laptops or iPhones can discover our HP wireless printer on the home Wi-Fi network!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning Faisal. I can inspect your Hub Pro local network configuration and subnet routing. Before we check your settings, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 47 Richmond Road, Sheffield, S13 8TB, and my security PIN is 2981. My printer IP address is 192.168.1.150.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Faisal, that confirms your account details. What happens when you try to print a test document from one of your laptops?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The print queue says 'Printer Offline' or 'Printer Not Found', even though the blue Wi-Fi light on the HP printer is glowing solid blue because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the printer connected to the main 2.4 gigahertz Wi-Fi network or the separate Guest network in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is connected to the primary Wi-Fi network, the exact same SSID that our laptops and phones are connected to so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a couple of minutes while I query your Hub Pro gateway configuration tables on our provisioning server across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Faisal. I have pulled up your Hub Pro profile. The wireless local area network settings have Client Isolation enabled by default to maintain optimal throughput and low latency across the regional distribution network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My wife and I run an architectural consultancy from home, and we have tender documents that must be printed and signed by courier in forty minutes! We are completely stuck and panicking! Why would your router ship with settings that break basic printing so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Client isolation is a baseline security protocol designed to prevent infected smart home devices from executing lateral network reconnaissance across consumer subnets in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I do not need a cybersecurity lecture, Liam! I need my HP printer to show up on my laptop so I can print our contract before the courier arrives since we depend heavily on this service for remote working and family communications every day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To enable peer-to-peer discovery across connected wireless clients, client isolation must be deactivated within the advanced gateway GUI across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you turn it off remotely from your screen right now because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Frontline technical support agents cannot alter private LAN subnet isolation flags remotely for customer privacy reasons to ensure your S-Net service operates reliably without unexpected dropped packets or connection faults.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then tell me exactly how to log into the Hub Pro and change the setting myself so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously local subnet isolation prevents broadcast packets like mDNS and Bonjour from crossing wireless access point interfaces so that your account records and provisioning parameters remain completely up to date.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand that, please just give me the IP address and admin login.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open an internet browser tab on your laptop and type 192.168.1.254 into the address bar.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typed 192.168.1.254. A page titled 'S-Net Hub Pro Manager' has loaded asking for the admin password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look at the removable plastic settings card slotted into the back of the Hub Pro router to find the admin password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got the card... Admin password is 'Echo-992-Delta'. Typing it in now and clicking Login.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once logged in, click on the 'Advanced Settings' tab along the top navigation bar.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicked Advanced Settings. It shows Wireless, Firewall, DHCP, and System.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on 'Wireless', and then select 'WLAN Configuration' from the sub-menu.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Selected WLAN Configuration. I see SSIDs and advanced toggles. Liam, I am having a complete panic attack right now! The courier van just pulled up outside! If this printer doesn't spit out the tender pages in three minutes, we lose a forty-thousand-pound contract!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Locate the toggle switch labeled 'AP Client Isolation' or 'Station Isolation'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found it! 'AP Client Isolation' is currently toggled to ON in green.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click that toggle to switch it to OFF, and then click 'Save Changes' at the bottom of the page.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Toggled to OFF and clicked Save Changes... The router page says 'Settings saved successfully.'

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What was that printer IP address again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I said earlier, it is 192.168.1.150.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now open your printer queue on your laptop and try printing your document again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening print queue... It says 'HP LaserJet Ready'! Clicking Print... Yes! I can hear the printer warming up and spitting out the pages right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And let us check an iPhone to verify that Apple AirPrint discovery is functioning across the wireless network as well.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Testing on my iPhone... Opened a PDF, tapped Share, tapped Print... Yes! The HP printer appeared instantly under AirPrint! Printing page two now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms mDNS and multicast Bonjour traffic are broadcasting freely between all your household devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What a relief! The tender contract is printed, signed, and ready for the courier. Thank you Liam.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you ever factory reset the Hub Pro in the future, remember that AP Client Isolation will default back to ON.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have written a note on the admin card: remember to disable AP Client Isolation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We have accessed your Hub Pro manager, deactivated AP Client Isolation, and confirmed both Windows and AirPrint discovery work normally.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything is working perfectly. You have saved my working day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other aspect of your Hub Pro wireless network I can help you with today, Faisal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your Hub Pro router will automatically optimize wireless channel selection during quiet hours overnight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will keep our Wi-Fi interference low from neighboring flats.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The dual-band antennas provide high throughput across both 2.4 and 5 gigahertz spectra.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The wireless speeds have been excellent across all our rooms.
